title: Laredo City Council votes 5-2 to explore pediatric care deal with DHR Health
excerpt: The Laredo City Council voted 5-2 on Monday to approve a non-binding letter of intent with DHR Health, opening a 60-day window to discuss a pediatric emergency facility, trauma center and neonatal intensive care unit on up to 8.5 acres at Laredo International Airport.
content:
The Laredo City Council voted 5-2 on Monday, November 9, to approve a non-binding letter of intent with DHR Health to discuss expanded pediatric care in Laredo, according to KGNS.

Councilmembers Dr. Tyler King and Melissa Cigarroa voted against the agreement. Mayor Pete Saenz also spoke against it, saying, “I’m not in support of this agreement.”

The letter of intent gives DHR Health a 60-day window to discuss a potential pediatric emergency facility, trauma center, neonatal intensive care unit (NICU), pediatric clinic and outpatient services. It does not commit the city or DHR Health to building a pediatric hospital.

Under the agreement, DHR Health would pay the costs of the project, while the city would commit to a $1-per-year lease for 40 years for up to 8.5 acres at Laredo International Airport, next to the new fire station, according to KGNS.

DHR Health CEO Dr. Alvaro Restrepo said DHR currently operates the only pediatric emergency room in Laredo. Laredo Medical Center CEO Jorge Leal said the hospital looks forward to continuing to work with the city to expand pediatric services for families in Laredo and the surrounding region.

The vote follows voters’ approval of Proposition 1 on November 3, a measure supporting pediatric care in Laredo. The Texas Legislature allocated $40 million during the 2025 session for pediatric care in Laredo, but the funds have not yet been allocated, and the city applied for state funding earlier this year, according to KGNS.

KGNS said it had contacted the City of Laredo and DHR Health for comment and had not heard back at the time of its report.

Sources: KGNS, November 10, 2026.
